inspiration: Two-stage drop roll: a group fires on an overall percent, then one item in the group is picked by walking cumulative chance values and stopping at the first hit (src/GameServer/World/Generics/NpcRewards.js:10-17). Easy to recreate as zone data with originals.

Spawn data as per-template coordinate lists with a bounds field and a loop over spawn points (src/GameServer/World/Generics/SpawnNpcs.js:12-14; data/Templates/Spawns/spawns.json:3-4). Matches the zones-as-data ruling and row 23.

Aggro is a per-creature flag plus a radius: a scan of nearby hostile NPCs within 500 units when the player is within a 5000-unit circle (src/GameServer/Actor/Generics/UpdateEnvironment.js:6 and 22; src/GameServer/Model/Npc.js:35).
Leash: once in combat, an NPC checks distance each interval and drops combat when the actor is 150 or more units away (src/GameServer/Npc/Npc.js:57-66). Shape to reuse for row 4 (leash).

Staggered replies: after a 1000-unit move, NPC info is re-sent with a random delay per NPC (utils.randomNumber(2000); the helper's range was not read) rather than in one burst (src/GameServer/Actor/Generics/UpdateEnvironment.js:9-11). Useful for the per-tick budget idea in row 18.
Skill levels stored as rows of power, mana, hp, item cost per level in one table (data/Skills/Active/active.json:5). Matches catalogue-as-data rows 20 and 21.
Dialogue as small HTML pages with bypass links (data/Html/126.html:4). A simple talk-menu shape; keep the menu structure, write our own text.

Defects to fix, not copy: the combat timeout builds a zero-coordinates object (src/GameServer/Npc/Npc.js:57-61) whose use was not read; a hard-coded z hack is marked TODO by the author (src/GameServer/Actor/Generics/UpdateEnvironment.js:24). Fix: keep the leash idea, and return to the spawn anchor by explicit zone data.

briefs.label: Leashed roaming guard (own label)
briefs.why: A hostile that waits near its anchor, engages when a player comes within a set radius, and gives up the chase at a fixed leash distance. Idea only: no art in the box, so the silhouette at 375 wide is for us to design.
briefs.keep: Radius-on-enter aggro; a leash distance that drops combat; a single hostile flag per creature record
briefs.change: Anchor is a zone-data point, not a coordinate table per class; leash ends with a visible walk-home and a short reset animation; a distinct original design, never a copy of any donor creature

briefs.label: Two-roll drop bundle (own label)
briefs.why: A drop reads as a ceremony: first a chance to drop anything at all, then one item from a weighted group. Gives a readable loot story.
briefs.keep: Overall chance gate then weighted pick; first match wins; item range min to max
briefs.change: Our drop uses rarity colour and a distinct sound cue; the weights live in zone data with a named table; the drop model is a new original, not the donor's item art
